paras: Hemidactylus bavazzanoi, also known commonly as Bavazzano's gecko, the Somali banded gecko, and  the Somali leaf-toed gecko,  is a species of lizard in the family Gekkonidae. The species is native to eastern Africa.
The specific name, bavazzanoi, is in honor of Italian botanist Renato Bavazzano.
H. bavazzanoi is found in southern Ethiopia, northeastern Kenya, and southern Somalia.
The preferred natural habitat of H. bavazzanoi is shrubland.

Medium-sized for its genus, H. bavazzanoi may attain a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 4 cm (1.6 in). Dorsally, it is pink with four black crossbands, a crescentic one on the neck, two on the body, and one on the base of the tail.
